history: Autódromo Max Mohr, commonly known as Ascurra, is a motorsport venue nestled in the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil. While primarily known for its rallycross configurations, the venue also hosts a variety of other motorsports events. The original construction aimed to bring international-caliber racing to the region, and although it hasn't hosted top-tier international championships consistently, it remains a vital hub for Brazilian motorsports. The Ascurra Dirt layout, a dedicated dirt track, has been a staple for regional rallycross and off-road competitions since the track opened. It provides a challenging and compact circuit for close-quarters racing, fostering intense battles and thrilling finishes. While specific national rallycross championships have been held here, Ascurra often serves as a crucial round in regional series, attracting a dedicated following of drivers and spectators alike.
atmosphere: The air crackles with anticipation as the cars line up on the grid for an Ascurra Dirt race. The roar of engines mixes with the cheers of the crowd, the scent of burning rubber and freshly tilled earth filling the nostrils. The setting sun casts long shadows across the track, highlighting the rooster tails of dirt kicked up by the accelerating cars. The compact nature of the circuit means the action is always close at hand, with every drift and bump amplified by the passionate Brazilian fans who line the fences, their energy infectious and their support unwavering.
trackCharacter: The Ascurra Dirt layout is a tight and technical dirt oval, demanding precision and car control above all else. At just 0.91km in length and featuring 8 turns, it's a high-intensity sprint from start to finish. Momentum is key, and drivers must be prepared to constantly wrestle with the car as they navigate the loose surface. The track's design encourages close racing and aggressive maneuvers, making it a true test of driving skill and nerve.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Pinheiro (Pine Tree Corner)
famousCorners.description: A wide, sweeping right-hander that requires a delicate balance of throttle and steering to maintain optimal speed.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining traction through the loose surface and avoiding running wide into the infield.

famousCorners.name: Cotovelo do Rio (River Elbow)
famousCorners.description: A tight, almost hairpin-like left turn that demands heavy braking and a quick change of direction.
famousCorners.challenge: Nailing the braking point and avoiding locking up the wheels on the approach.

famousCorners.name: Curva da Mata (Forest Corner)
famousCorners.description: A medium-speed right-hand sweeper that offers a slight elevation change.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining momentum through the corner and avoiding losing grip on the exit.

famousCorners.name: O Cascalho (The Gravel)
famousCorners.description: A section of the track that features a transition from hard-packed dirt to loose gravel, testing the car's stability and the driver's adaptability.
famousCorners.challenge: Adjusting driving style to compensate for the changing grip levels and avoiding getting bogged down in the gravel.

famousCorners.name: Curva da Torcida (The Crowd's Corner)
famousCorners.description: The final corner before the finish line, often packed with spectators and a prime location for last-lap heroics.
famousCorners.challenge: Carrying maximum speed through the turn while maintaining a clean line and avoiding contact with other cars.

keyFactors: Quick reactions to changing track conditions
overtakingSpots: Into Cotovelo do Rio (River Elbow) under braking
Exiting Curva do Pinheiro (Pine Tree Corner) with better momentum
Into Curva da Torcida (The Crowd's Corner) on the final lap

weatherNotes: The weather in Ascurra can be unpredictable, with sudden rain showers being common. Rain can quickly turn the Ascurra Dirt layout into a mud bath, significantly reducing grip and increasing the challenge for drivers. Conversely, dry and sunny conditions can lead to a dusty track, making visibility a major concern. The ever-changing weather conditions add another layer of complexity to the racing.
drivingAdvice: On the Ascurra Dirt layout, a smooth and consistent driving style is crucial. Avoid sudden changes in direction or throttle input, as this can easily upset the car's balance on the loose surface. Focus on maximizing traction out of the corners and maintaining momentum throughout the lap. Be prepared to adjust your driving style based on the changing track conditions and don't be afraid to get aggressive in overtaking maneuvers.
famousRaces: Santa Catarina Rallycross Championship: A regional series that has consistently held races at Ascurra Dirt, attracting top drivers from the state.
Brazilian Rallycross Cup: A national-level event that has featured thrilling battles and dramatic finishes on the challenging dirt track.
Local Club Races: Ascurra Dirt is a regular host to amateur racing events, providing a platform for aspiring drivers to hone their skills.
localCulture: Ascurra is a charming town with a strong agricultural heritage. The local cuisine features hearty dishes made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The people are warm and welcoming, and motorsports are a popular pastime. The paddock at Ascurra is a vibrant and friendly atmosphere, with drivers, mechanics, and fans mingling and sharing their passion for racing. The local culture adds to the unique charm of the Ascurra racing experience.
